title: The Low-Information Diet: Cultivating Selective Ignorance
coreMove: Protect attention by pulling just-in-time, actionable facts for real decisions, while refusing news, browsing, and reading that cannot change your next move.

exampleSpecs.audience: solo operators who confuse updates with preparation
exampleSpecs.stakes: finish the draft or spend the best hour on headlines
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist starts a one-week media fast before television news consumes the work block

exampleSpecs.audience: operators tempted to stockpile general research
exampleSpecs.stakes: buy the needed tool or keep reading for imaginary futures
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist uses the just-in-time filter to pull only actionable facts

exampleSpecs.stakes: scan all morning or ask for the concise update
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist asks an informed person for the update instead of monitoring feeds

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who might flatten the idea into anti-learning
exampleSpecs.stakes: protect deep study or misuse the diet as an excuse
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist separates selective ignorance from contempt for learning

exampleSpecs.audience: professionals who mistake anxiety for usefulness
exampleSpecs.stakes: finish the client mockup or keep absorbing distant headlines
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist checks whether headlines relate to an action under control

exampleSpecs.audience: operators whose feeds interrupt planning work
exampleSpecs.stakes: plan staffing or let pushed updates define the hour
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist replaces pushed information with a pulled query
